0.content:
Alice, founder of the Hexenzirkel, found Nicole wandering after the angels' fall. She listened to all her stories over a drink and a bag of biscuits, asked whether they were true, and declared that a mage and an angel "match perfectly". She invited Nicole to her brand-new club and sealed the "mages' pact" by pressing her last piece of candy into Nicole's hand, without waiting for an answer Nicole could not give. Nicole says Alice "corrupted" her. Alice compared her to the sea's daughter who traded her voice for legs: "the daughter of the heavens sacrificed her voice to become human."

Alice gives Nicole jobs and pranks her. She told her to sound mysterious and noble when speaking to strangers, made her the Nod-Krai "communication hub" ("You love talking, don't you?"), and wrote self-introduction magic that hijacks her introductions. She once told Nicole not to imagine stubbing a toe with a toothpick under the nail, just to hear how far her unconscious scream would carry; everyone within a hundred metres lost their inner voice for days. Nicole jokes about bad-mouthing her and refuses to actually do it.

1.content:
At the Hexenzirkel's tea parties Nicole is the quiet, mysterious one, at least on the surface. She knows everyone's tea (Alice three sugars, Anya one, Barbeloth none). She once asked the mages what the world was for: M (Andersdotter) said not to give it human motives, O (Octavia) said "to resist destruction", B (Barbeloth) didn't care, and R (Rhinedottir) thought it would make a nice test. Alice answered by taking her sightseeing at the border of other worlds.

The mages' group farewell "prophecy" to J, a member leaving to marry, carried four signatures; N's was "a guide who will never get lost". Alice described her as a woman who made "this world's direction and order her subject of study". Nicole met Rhinedottir in person only after Rhinedottir turned twenty; Alice carried letters until then. In the Character Details story Nicole tells her "long, long ago" tales while Andersdotter tries to write them down, Barbeloth hints they may attract "visitors" from on high, and Rhinedottir says she would like to meet them.

2.comment: Nicole: The angels' fall and Nicole's bargain
2.content:
The angels were made to guide humanity. After the rebellion of the war of funerary flame, the heavens punished all of them. Those who refused to give up power lost their wisdom and became beasts or dragons such as Ursa. Others became Seelie, sank into the sea, hid in the sands or melded with the earth. Nicole surrendered half her wisdom and half her power. She offered her voice as a "bargaining chip", since "the heavens demanded silence and punishment", and kept her form. She now calls herself a human who lost her voice.

She says she wasn't smarter than the other angels, only bold. She would have liked silver scales had she become a dragon. She calls giving up her wings "not a fall from grace" and her silence "the strength to listen before judging". She believes humans hold divine potential.

Her eldest sister Koitar, once closest to the Lord of the Sky, taught that the laws must not be tested. Nicole believed it until heaven's grace fell silent on her mid-sentence and she saw the Celestial Nail erase city after city. In Celestia, she says, inside and outside do not relate normally, much like a Serenitea Pot.

3.comment: Nicole: Columbina's name and the Hyperborean portal
3.content:
When the Traveler sought a way to return the fading Moon Goddess beyond the false sky, Nicole explained that Hyperboreans after the war of funerary flame had built kuuvahki structures to contact the moons, only to learn the three goddesses were dead. Their ritual could become a portal. She found phantoms to project into the past, tested candidates by kuuvahki infusion ("Cheating the system is much easier than trying to hide from it") and chose the Traveler, Lauma and Arlecchino. In the ruins she saw that Columbina had never had a true name, and that one could simply be given: "Names are anchors that connect us to the world."

She explained the murals: Nibelung raised the three moons; when he returned with the Abyss's power he imprisoned the sisters and turned the moons into weapons; the Heavenly Principles shattered two and flung the third beyond the sky. She could not identify a "he" the phantoms mentioned. The Wanderer later found the phantoms' history differed from hers because of Dottore's meddling.

4.content: "Mr. Nine", the famous author Fischl idolises, is a pen name. Nicole wanted to be an author but found writing too tedious, so she told her stories to an old Seelie friend, a fellow former angel. The Seelie possessed sleeping would-be authors to write them, recovering her own capacity for speech along the way. Fischl found the Seelie in Nod-Krai. Nicole admitted that one "Mr. Nine" book held a half-true metaphor for the creation of life, which is how Fischl made Oz: "70 percent made-up, 30 percent true." Nicole insists the book was her idea; now that the Seelie has her intellect back, they argue about plot and first authorship.

5.comment: Nicole: Hyperborea and the girl who asked questions
5.content: As envoy to a Hyperborean city, Nicole sat in a temple answering a brilliant girl's questions about falling fruit, thunder and the moon's orbit, secretly cramming at night to stay ahead. The townsfolk had once chained the girl to stop dangerous questions; she carved equations into the floor with her shackles. Generations later her descendant asked what the world was for. Nicole had no answer, and at that moment heaven's grace stopped responding. She led the survivors away from the falling Nail and tried to teach them to live from nothing, in a land shrouded by a "pale calamity". When the girl asked again, Nicole said: "I don't know."

6.comment: Nicole: The Frost Moon and Varka
6.content: While Columbina was lost, Nicole voiced a theory that Luonnotar was an "anchor" Columbina left behind. When Grand Master Varka admitted he was out of his depth, she reminded him Teyvat "gave us you" and that angels believe every human special. He invoked the terms he had won in the three-way talks with the Hexenzirkel, though they concerned protecting Mondstadt. She agreed: "The mages have heard the knights' plea." She gave him a gift and later helped him and Arlecchino pull the Frost Moon below the false sky. Afterward she warned that the disaster had made Teyvat easier to detect from outside and sent the Traveler to the docks to say goodbye to friends.

7.comment: Nicole: Collei, Nabu Malikata and Liloupar
7.content: After Nod-Krai, Collei dreamed Sumeru's identities were scrambled. Nicole spoke into her mind, called it a premonition, and told her to tell Nahida and the Traveler. Near Aaru she taught Collei an ancient verse ("I am a spirit created at the beginning...") that made attacking desert Jinn stand down. At the Temple of Silence she told her the truth: Collei carries a fragment of Nabu Malikata, "an angel... just like me", which kept warning her. She added that this did not change who Collei is. Afterward she invited Collei to Windrise, where her friend Liloupar asked to absorb those remains. Nicole checked that both were sure. Then she declared it a happy ending, and said her own wishes included protecting the people she meets.

8.comment: Nicole: Nefer and the Sumeru crisis
8.content:
Sensing a crisis in Sumeru, Nicole visited Nefer in Nod-Krai, offered to pay for the trip (or in sculptures), and arrived just before Irminsul sealed the nation off. She thought the barrier was a defence built into Irminsul. She knew Nefer's power came from the Ibis King, a former Moon Envoy, but would not pry into her past. She also told Nefer that when the object of a hatred is gone, the emotion fades into a void worse than love or hate. During the counterattack she reported Fatui in Sumeru City, watched from the Eternal Oasis, and guided the Traveler and Wanderer out of Dottore's traps inside Irminsul until he cut her off. She later moved Nahida's connection to Irminsul onto Aaru.

Talking with Nefer, she admitted she fears the word "era" and the endless flow of time, because time "renders all memories insignificant". Comparing herself with Collei made her want more than before. "Guiding humans to make the miracles in their hearts a reality... that is my miracle." She also bonded with Faruzan over heroic statues and resolved to sculpt a heroic squirrel pointing to the sky.

9.comment: Nicole: Mage N's voice in Sumeru and Fontaine
9.content: After the Wanderer erased himself from Irminsul (3.3), a voice told the Traveler that Teyvat's fate cannot easily be changed, "but human hearts can". In Fontaine (4.2) an ornate red teacup appeared at the Traveler's table. Calling herself N, "a mage who wanders the world", she said the prophecy would be fulfilled, a "history of the future", while hinting that prophecies are the future seen by gods, who do not see every hidden corner. She told the Traveler to play their part and thanked them for the tea. She later admitted the air of mystery was Alice's advice.

10.comment: Nicole: Sculptures, chests and the Witch's Lodge
10.content: Nicole sculpts to keep records and leaves stone squirrels (her metaphor for humanity) wherever she lives. Angels "just can't resist" guiding adventurers to treasure; she buries chests behind riddles, and the chest matters more to her than what is in it ("some Mora, and perhaps a few cabbages"). She turned her secret Witch's Lodge in Nod-Krai into rooms of puzzles and treasure for her friends, starting with a miniature "Great Mage's Tea Party" with an animated Mandragora statue. Explaining her delight, she said angels once felt their strongest joy on completing a duty, and that she does not consider this pitiable.

11.comment: Nicole: Witch's Homework: The Role of a Guide
11.content: With Barbeloth meditating to rebalance hydromancy shaken by the moon's shift, Octavia away, Rhinedottir unreachable and Alice guarding the border, Nicole had to supervise everyone's homework. Barbeloth and Alice had already written her own: "Nicole will fulfill her duty." She led the Traveler through Seelie Courts ("the Seelie and I used to be angels, so we're old colleagues") to places from Venti's homework and from that of "the child" with his "lupical". Barbeloth and Alice had secretly built a Seelie Court in Nicole's own Witch's Lodge (Alice had borrowed the key), the symbol of a finished guidance. Sitting down there inscribed her story in the dictionary and made her tutor for future homework.

12.content: During a limited-time 6.4 event, Nicole and Alice built a "memory bubble" replaying the Traveler's first days in Mondstadt, meant as an experience "even a child can complete". Nicole effectively directed it. She trimmed complicated parts, fixed glitches such as Fatui costumes failing to load, gave hints through communication magic and asked the cast not to go off script. She kept actors such as Mika and Fischl to their lines. Alice left the testing to her to play with Klee.

13.comment: Nicole: Zibai and the other angels
13.content: Nicole knows the fates of her sisters. The Seelie are former angels who kept the instinct to guide. Ursa the Drake was one who chose power and lost wisdom. Nabu Malikata survives only in remains. The Lord of the Night in Natlan kept less power than Nicole because of a long-term duty. Zibai, a gifted angel tied to the Archangel, was constantly praised by the elders, and Nicole would "rather not" meet her. She thinks some sisters may have secretly kept copies of the "books" from Celestia's closed library. She remembers an elder sister describing Lang-Gan, where groups of people learned different skills separately under that city's angel.

key: Little Witch and the Undying Fire
14.comment: Nicole: Klee, Durin and the children
14.content: Nicole adores Klee but may not speak in her head, because Alice worries about her brain development. She asks the Traveler to put in a good word. She wrote Volume 5 of The Little Witch and the Undying Fire. She calls Durin Anya's final masterpiece and swore to protect him. In Proof of Strength (6.6), Lohen's homework, Durin seems to have dropped his copy of her script, spoiling her grand entrance. Prune is hunting her on Alice's suggestion, and Nicole hopes to go treasure hunting with the girl if found.

15.content: Long after the fall, Nicole felt the world's rules shift when Visions appeared and wanted one, though she knew where they lead. Heaven ignored her until the Lord of the Night told her the angels had been erased from the world's design. So she made herself part of human lives: sculpture commissions paid into treasure chests, silent guidance for the lost, clues for confused scholars. Helping an old man finally tipped the balance. Holding the Pyro Vision up to eclipse Celestia, she told her Creator that it finally saw her as human, and she would live "a little more freely and boldly". She says being human is being free and "not so free".
